summary.text: 房 combines 戶, a dwelling-related semantic element, with 方 as a phonetic element. A traditional gloss defines it as a room beside the main room; recorded uses include “room” and “house.”

formation.text: The received analysis treats 房 as phonosemantic: 戶 contributes the dwelling-related category and 方 supplies a sound cue. The gloss “room beside the main room” is recorded historically; a further meaning contribution from 方 (“side”) remains uncertain.

components.text: 戶 is the semantic element in the received analysis, linking 房 with a dwelling or room. The seal-style rendering places it above 方. In a Chu form, 戶 has a local graphic form; an optional short upper stroke is described as decorative.
方 is the phonetic element in the received analysis. Its possible additional contribution “side” is uncertain. Historical readings of 方 approximately match 房 in the cited systems.

sound.text: In Middle Chinese transcription, 房 and a corresponding reading of 方 are both bjang; 方 also has pjang. Baxter–Sagart reports 房 *[Cə-N-]paŋ and 方 *baŋ for the corresponding reading, while Zhengzhang gives *baŋ for both. These are system-specific reconstructions or transcriptions, not direct recordings.
sound.system: Middle Chinese transcription; Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese; Zhengzhang Old Chinese

history.text: The curated seal-script-style rendering shows 戶 above 方. It is a modern redraw representing the form tradition transmitted in the Shuowen Jiezi, not an ancient artifact image. Historical-form categories include Chu manuscript, small seal, and Shuowen forms, but their detailed graphic sequence is not established here.

A reported catalogue places the graph’s first appearance in Warring States writing; this is a cautious attestation boundary, not proof that the graph did not exist earlier. A Chu-script analysis describes a form of 戶 in 房 on Baoshan slip 149, with an optional short upper stroke as decoration. No corruption or sequence of graphic changes is established.

uncertainties.text: The traditional side-room gloss and recorded house and room senses do not establish a complete chronology. The early phrase 由房 has competing interpretations, so its precise sense remains unresolved.
方’s phonetic role is supported by approximate historical sound correspondences; its proposed additional contribution “side” remains speculative.
Tibetan and Burmese comparisons have been proposed, but their cognacy and chronology are not established here.

senses.text: The traditional lexicographic gloss defines 房 as a room beside the main room. This is an attested historical interpretation, not proof that it was the character’s original meaning.

senses.period: attested by the Three Kingdoms period in a cited literary example
senses.text: A cited Three Kingdoms-era poem uses 空房, “empty room.” This attests the room sense by that period, but does not establish how it developed from the side-room sense.
“House” or “dwelling” is a recorded current sense. Its chronological relation to the side-room and room senses is unresolved.

limitations.text: The evidence supports these senses but does not establish their full chronology or a transition linking them. Early material for 由房 is reported, but its precise interpretation remains disputed.
